audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Trundle all seven stages in a matchup he loses at 42.99% over 107 games — and five of the seven why-texts underneath it describe Sejuani winning. Levels 4-5, 6, first item and 2+ items all read as her stages in prose while the card said Trundle.
audit.why: This is the largest disagreement in the slice: a 43% matchup presented as a clean 7-0 sweep. Everything after level 3 in the text is about her CC chain beating your zone, so the chart was contradicting its own copy at every stage.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Trundle / Trundle / Skill / Skill / Sejuani / Sejuani / Sejuani in both layers, matching the packet's stage read and the existing prose.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the level-6 spike calls Glacial Prison 'a point-and-click AOE stun'. It is a thrown bola at 1300 range that stuns the first champion hit, on a 120/105/90s cooldown.
audit.why: 'Point-and-click' tells the player the stun is unavoidable, so he stops trying to dodge it — and it is the single ability that decides whether the level-6 fight happens at all. Its 120s rank-1 cooldown is also the biggest window either champion has.
audit.corrected: Glacial Prison described as a dodgeable projectile with its 120s rank-1 cooldown, plus Arctic Assault (18s), Winter's Wrath (9s) and Permafrost (a flat 1.5s) all given real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three hard errors. (a) 'She has no gap-close, so you set the engagement distance' — Arctic Assault is a 650-range charge that knocks enemies into the air, 18s at rank 1, and the matchup never names it once. (b) Fury of the North is described as a 'shield [that] absorbs burst'; it is Armor, Magic Resist and IMMUNITY TO SLOWS, and it lets her shatter a stunned enemy for massive magic damage. (c) Chomp is repeatedly said to slow her attack speed; it saps attack damage and slows movement.
audit.why: The slow immunity is the decisive interaction of the entire matchup and it was completely absent. Trundle's only two forms of control are Chomp's slow and Pillar of Ice's slow, and Frost Armor turns both off while it is up. Combined with (a), the old text told the player he controls the distance in a lane where she opens with a knock-up charge into a slow-immune trade.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor's slow immunity and stun-shatter written into early, mid, whys[1], whys[3] and breakdown.cooldowns; Arctic Assault named as her engage; the attack-speed claim corrected to attack damage in four places.

audit.whatIsWrong: late says to avoid Subjugating Sejuani because she 'has limited resistances to steal anyway'.
audit.why: Fury of the North grants her Armor and Magic Resist on top of a tank build, and Subjugate steals a percent of exactly those two stats plus Health. She is close to the best possible Subjugate target in her own team, not the worst.
audit.corrected: Rewritten: ult her while Frost Armor is up, which is when the percent steal is worth most. The 5v5 advice to prioritise a frontliner is kept, because it can be someone else's frontliner.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Trade only when Glacial Prison is on cooldown' with no cooldown given, and 'Permafrost's stun cooldown shortens with ranks' — Permafrost is a flat 1.5 seconds at every rank.
audit.why: What actually ranks up is her Frost application through Winter's Wrath (9s down to 5s), not the stun itself. A player waiting for a Permafrost cooldown that does not exist will never take the trade.
audit.corrected: Corrected to the real cadence: Permafrost fires the instant Frost stacks cap, so the cooldown you play around is Winter's Wrath, and the big window is Glacial Prison's 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Chomp's AD steal and AS debuff win short trades before Sejuani can stack Permafrost — this is your clearest damage window.
edits.after: Chomp's AD sap and movement slow win short trades before Sejuani can stack Frost — this is your clearest damage window in the lane.

edits.before: Sejuani's R comes online: a point-and-click AOE stun that interrupts your Frozen Domain all-in and lets her punish any overcommit with a full CC chain.
edits.after: Glacial Prison (120s at rank 1) is a thrown bola, not point-and-click — it stuns the first champion hit at 1300 range, and her passive shatters what it stuns.

edits.before: Land Q Chomp on Sejuani's every step-up to steal her AD and slow her attack speed before Permafrost stacks build
edits.after: Land Chomp on her every step-up to sap her AD, but expect the slow to do nothing while Frost Armor is up

edits.before: Cast R Subjugate early in any committed fight to drain her armor and MR before her W percent-HP damage chips you through your own resistance gains
edits.after: Cast Subjugate early in a committed fight, and cast it while Frost Armor is up — that is when her armour and MR are highest to steal

edits.before: Stack Permafrost on you through any ability or auto hit, then land E to stun you out of Frozen Domain and break your W-empowered pattern
edits.after: Open with Arctic Assault (18s at rank 1) for the knock-up, stack Frost with Winter's Wrath, then Permafrost to stun you out of Frozen Domain

edits.before: Q Chomp bites her AD before she has frost stacks loaded, and the flat damage plus AS slow wins the very first auto-trade pattern at level 1.
edits.after: Chomp bites her AD before she has Frost stacks loaded, and the flat damage wins the first auto-trade pattern at level 1 outright.

edits.before: W Frozen Domain gives you move speed and healing from passive kills before Sejuani has reliable frost stacking or her E cooldown short enough to punish your zone fighting.
edits.after: Frozen Domain gives you move speed and King's Tribute healing before she has reliable Frost stacking — but note that Frost Armor makes her immune to your slows while it holds.

edits.before: Sejuani's frost application becomes more consistent at higher levels and Permafrost's stun cooldown shortens with ranks — she can now reliably interrupt your Frozen Domain window mid-trade, erasing your duel advantage.
edits.after: Her Frost application gets consistent as Winter's Wrath drops toward 5s, and Permafrost fires on a flat 1.5s the instant stacks cap — so she interrupts your Frozen Domain whenever the stacks are there.

edits.before: You win the very early levels on raw kit pressure alone: Chomp bites AD off Sejuani's auto attempts and the AS slow stops her from quickly stacking Permafrost with consecutive autos. Drop W at your feet and keep trades short — bite once, weave an auto inside the zone, then back off before she reaches three frost stacks and fires E. She has no gap-close, so you set the engagement distance. Respect the E stun range and never stand directly on top of her when a frost stack is already showing on your health bar.
edits.after: You win the very early levels on raw kit pressure: Chomp bites AD off Sejuani's auto attempts and the flat damage beats hers before Frost stacks exist. Drop W at your feet and keep trades short — bite once, weave an auto inside the zone, then step out before her stacks cap and Permafrost fires. Two things the lane is easy to misplay: Arctic Assault is a 650-range charge that knocks you into the air, so she does have a gap-close, and Frost Armor makes her immune to slows, so neither Chomp nor Pillar controls her until damage breaks it.

edits.before: The matchup turns at Level 6. Her R Glacial Prison is a fast-moving AOE projectile that stuns on direct hit and slows on edge — it interrupts your Frozen Domain all-in completely if she lands it. Sejuani's W Winter's Wrath deals percent-current-HP damage twice per cast, meaning her chip damage ignores the armor you build or drain from Subjugate. You can still use R to drain her resists and gain meaningful durability, but she answers by dealing percent-HP damage through whatever armor you steal. Trade only when Glacial Prison is on cooldown, and use Pillar of Ice to cut off her escape or break her charge angle rather than to cage her in — her CC will outlast yours if you overcommit.
edits.after: The matchup turns at Level 6. Glacial Prison is a bola thrown up to 1300 range that stuns the first champion it hits, and her passive shatters a stunned target for heavy magic damage — so the stun is a damage amplifier, not just a lockdown, and it is dodgeable. Its cooldown is 120s at rank 1, which is the largest window in the lane: trade inside it. Before that, play around Winter's Wrath (9s at rank 1) rather than Permafrost, because Permafrost is a flat 1.5 seconds and fires the moment Frost stacks cap. Use Pillar of Ice to break her Arctic Assault angle rather than to cage her, and remember Frost Armor's slow immunity: your control only lands after she has taken damage.

edits.before: Late game Sejuani's kit is purpose-built for 5v5 and she outscales your individual duel threat. Her R stun sets up free kills for her entire team, her W percent-HP shreds tanks — including the stat-buffed Trundle post-Subjugate — and her passive Fury of the North shield absorbs burst. Your role is to Subjugate the other team's frontliner in fights (not Sejuani specifically, who has limited resistances to steal anyway), use Pillar to disrupt her R angle before she fires, and splitpush to exploit the map while she is occupied. Do not 1v1 Sejuani after 25 minutes unless Glacial Prison is confirmed on cooldown.
edits.after: Late game Sejuani's kit is purpose-built for 5v5 and she outscales your individual duel threat. Glacial Prison sets up free kills for her whole team, and Fury of the North gives her armour, magic resist and slow immunity rather than a shield. That resist bonus is the point for you: Subjugate steals a percent of Armor and Magic Resist, so if you do commit to her, commit while Frost Armor is up. In fights, ulting whichever frontliner is deepest still pays best, and Pillar of Ice disrupts her walk-up angle. Do not 1v1 her after 25 minutes unless Glacial Prison is confirmed down.

edits.before: - Sejuani Permafrost: matchup-defining — Her stun after Frost stacks. Don't get stacked + stunned. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Glacial Prison (R): 120/105/90s, a dodgeable bola. - Winter's Wrath (W): 9/8/7/6/5s — the Frost cadence you play around.

edits.before: Track Sejuani's Permafrost: Her stun after Frost stacks. Don't get stacked + stunned. When it is down — Bite + W-zone duel.
edits.after: Frost Armor gives her slow immunity and the resists Subjugate steals. Permafrost is flat 1.5s — play around Winter's Wrath.

edits.before: Pillar closes the kit — use it behind Sejuani to deny disengage, or between you and Permafrost to break her pattern.
edits.after: Pillar of Ice closes your kit, but Frost Armor's slow immunity blunts it — drop it behind her after damage breaks it.

edits.before: Q ranks raise the bite damage and the AD steal. Keep trading in W; if Sejuani stands in your domain trading evenly, she is losing.
edits.after: Chomp ranks up, but her Frost application does too. Winter's Wrath falling toward 5s is what lets Permafrost interrupt your zone.

edits.before: Subjugate online — the 1v1 is yours into almost anyone the moment Sejuani commits. R early in the all-in so the drained resists count for the whole fight.
edits.after: Glacial Prison arrives with Subjugate, and hers wins the exchange: a landed bola stuns you out of Frozen Domain and her passive shatters you for it.

edits.before: Trinity Force is the duel spike — Spellblade procs off every Chomp. Force Sejuani to answer you in the side lane.
edits.after: Her first tank item pushes the CC chain past your healing. Fight only on the 120-second Glacial Prison window.

edits.before: With two items you out-duel Sejuani whenever R is up. The only loss condition left is fighting with Subjugate down — track it like she tracks Permafrost.
edits.after: Two items deep her CC chain outlasts Subjugate. Take the side lane instead, and Pillar of Ice her walk-up angle rather than trying to cage her.

notes: UNVERIFIED, LEFT IN PLACE: this matchup asserts in six separate fields (spikes[2], spikes[3], wants.foe[1], mid, whys[5], whys[6], late) that Winter's Wrath deals percent-current-HP or percent-max-HP damage that bypasses armour. Riot's Winter's Wrath text says only 'swings her mace twice, dealing damage, slowing enemies and applying Frost stacks' — no percent-health component — and Sejuani's kit file carries no percentHealth flag. I did not restate the claim in anything I rewrote, but I also did not delete the six existing lines, because if the percent-health scaling is real the advice built on it is right and I have no source here either way. This needs one check against the live tooltip; if it is wrong, those six fields are the place to fix it. Also unverified and not written: whether Pillar of Ice's terrain stops Arctic Assault's charge.
